text: The three notice decision operations of the D7.1 approval are published on /api/recovery/comms/v1 as POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve, POST /notices/{noticeId}/regenerate and POST /notices/{noticeId}/hold, with decisionLogEntryId in the request of approve and hold, reasonCode on hold, templateCode on regenerate, the notice as the answer and the 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 set of section 12.1.
why: The legacy approves, changes and rejects through three Java methods of the P6 published interface, and neither the TSD P6 endpoint inventory nor the Ownership Map P6 row holds a notice-state operation, so the surface has to be fixed by the contract of the two services.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12 (NoticeApi.approve, regenerate, hold); TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Ownership Map v1 P6 REST operations; RWB-P7-E2014-CON; Template and Rules v1 R4 naming rules
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead and the solution architect confirm the three paths and their requests when the rwb-comms API file is baselined with RWB-P7-E2014-CON.
impact: The approval screen of rwb-decision builds against the three operations and their fake; a path change after the baseline breaks both stories and the SIT run.

text: The reference of the approval entry that moved a notice is the nullable column notice.decision_log_entry_id in rwb_comms, added by this story with a unique index and written by approve and hold; it stays null on a notice that no approval has moved.
why: Both decision calls of the legacy carry the decision log entry identifier and TSD P6 T3.1 gives the notice table no column for it, so the link between a notice and the approval that moved it has no home in the target data model.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (notice field list DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-034); Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12 (decisionLogEntryId) and section 11 (DF-DEC-053 on approval)
confirm: The solution architect and the P6 data steward add the column to the logical data model for rwb_comms at the next revision of the data dictionary.
impact: A notice can name the entry that approved or held it, and the panel can show the approver of a held notice without reading the approval table of P7.

text: A change of template variant regenerates on the same notice row: document_id and template_id move to the chosen Approved variant, the standard version column increments, and the previous document stays in rwb-document with the template version it was made from, so the approval keeps one notice identity.
why: The legacy says only that the new notice version replaces the proposed one on the approval, and the notice table holds single-valued document_id and template_id with no version chain, so neither the identity of the notice nor the fate of the superseded document is fixed by a source.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 7, AC2 and section 9; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-017, DF-LEG-031); FSD P6 Communications v3 AC-ALT-P6-007-01
confirm: The solution architect and the owners of rwb-comms and rwb-document confirm the one-row rule and the document versioning when the two contracts are baselined.
impact: The approval's source_ref stays valid across a change; if a new notice row were created instead, the approval would have to be repointed and the legacy criterion of one approved version would need a new key.

text: The notice answer carries id, caseId, documentId, noticeType, state, templateCode, templateVersion, templateState, approvedAt and decisionLogEntryId, read from notice and template in rwb_comms, with no personal field; the template state values are DRAFT, APPROVED and WITHDRAWN.
why: The appendix names the answer Notice with no property list, while the approval panel must show the template code and version and must know that the version has been withdrawn, and the notice row holds only template_id.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.2 (API-P6-002) and T3.1; Legacy RWB-E2-014 AC6, AC10 and section 12; RWB-P7-E2014-CON
confirm: The P6 and P7 tech leads confirm the summary shape in RWB-P7-E2014-CON before the screen contract is frozen.
impact: The panel can be composed from one notice read plus the route's own facts; a missing template state would force a second call and leave the withdrawn-template refusal to the route alone.

text: The three notice decision operations are declared as Litigation right A with scope applied and enforced at gateway-bff through the rwb-access contract, and rwb-decision calls them with its service identity plus the approver identifier and the decision entry reference in the request; no DP-08 row and no rwb-access contract is added to this key.
why: TSD P6 T6.2 requires every endpoint to declare an area and a right, the inventory declares none for the three operations, and the caller is a service and not the browser, so both the right and the way the approver is named have to be settled.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1 and T6.2; appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 10; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-08 and DP-11
confirm: The solution architect and the platform route owner confirm the declaration and the invocation model when the rwb-comms API file is baselined.
impact: A role without the right is refused at the edge with MSG-P4-002; the record still names the approver of rwb-decision, so the notice move is attributable without a second identity system inside the service.

text: The build row of this slice stays empty as the plan fixes it: the platform contracts that the patterns name are already dependencies of RWB-P6-E1052-CON and of the published libraries, and the two rwb-case contract reads of DP-06 and DP-07 are reached the same way; the fakes of section 12.8 stand in for them until the C list is extended.
why: The plan records H empty and one C row, while the pattern table adds six platform contracts and two rwb-case contracts; a story may not invent a build row that the plan does not carry, and a missing row does not block a Day-1 start.
read: Plan split slice RWB-P6-E2014-APP; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R5.7; RWB-P6-E1052-CON
confirm: The delivery lead extends the C list of the slice at the next plan revision and confirms that the notice contract baseline carries the platform rows.
impact: The story starts on Day 1 against published contracts and fakes; a platform contract that slips delays the fake, not the plan.

text: Every notice move writes one local decision record through the decision-record library with decision code D7.1, the rule in force (R-LIT-03 on approve, R-LIT-04 on a withdrawn template), the notice and case IDs, the template code and version, the state from and to, the reason code where one applies, the approver and the approval entry reference, and the record is relayed on rwb.decision-record.v1 in the same transaction as the notice row; the approval entry of rwb-decision stays the entry of the approval.
why: The TSD says the module writes through the decision log of P7 and the legacy passes the identifier of the entry P7 already wrote, while the target library writes locally and relays centrally; without a rule the fail-closed behaviour of the move cannot be stated or tested.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T2 and T4; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 12 and section 11; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03; ADR-022
confirm: The solution architect and the P7 decision-record owner confirm that two entries per approval — the approval entry and the notice-move entry — are accepted by the central ledger.
impact: A move that cannot be recorded changes nothing and answers 503; the central ledger holds the approval and the notice move as two linked records of the same decision.

text: The hold reason values REFUSED_BY_APPROVER and TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN are fixed as the value set of hold_reason by this story until LOV-HOLD-REASON is published in the reference data of rwb-case, and the feature switch keeps the legacy key rwb.decision.notice-approval, read by both services.
why: hold_reason carries no list of values in TSD P6 T3.1 and T3.2, and the legacy feature flag is named on the decision module while the operations it closes belong to rwb-comms, so neither the value set nor the key ownership has a source.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-032) and T3.2; Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 9 and section 13; FSD P6 Communications v3 AC-EXC-P6-001-02
confirm: The business analyst of P6 publishes LOV-HOLD-REASON and the platform feature-flag owner confirms the switch key.
impact: A check constraint on hold_reason holds the two known values and the SIT fixtures use them; a renamed switch would close the three operations for both services at once.
